w10_T4_001763: A bakery filled 5 ovens early in the morning, and each oven produced 163 rolls. Before the morning rush was over, 113 of those rolls had been sold at the counter. During the afternoon a caterer collected 382 rolls for a wedding. In the evening every roll still in the shop was cut into 8 small pieces for the buffet trays. The baker, who has worked here for a dozen years, times his proving in minutes rather than hours. How many small pieces did the evening's cutting produce?
w10_T4_001766: A garden centre stored 134 boxes of tulip bulbs, and each box contained 4 bulbs. The team planted 308 of those bulbs along the front drive. Every bulb still left in the boxes was potted up and later produced 8 flowers. A neighbouring bed added 54 more flowers to the same display. Florists bought 322 flowers from the display before the weekend. The greenhouse cost 9500 pounds to build, and its heating is billed in minutes of running time rather than hours. How many flowers are left in the display?
w10_T4_001770: A hardware distributor holds 127 pallets, and each pallet carries 8 cartons. A supplier delivered 26 loose cartons of exactly the same kind. Every carton in the store contains 7 boxes, and a customer returned 69 unopened boxes that went onto the shelves too. Each box holds 8 packets, and every packet contains 7 drawing pins. The distributor has been supplying the trade for a dozen years. How many drawing pins are in the store?
w10_T4_001772: In the morning a warehouse split its 176 sacks of flour equally between 2 vans. The driver of the first van delivered 70 sacks before lunch. In the early afternoon a bakery returned 45 surplus sacks, which went back into that same van. Each sack still in the van holds 9 kilograms of flour. During the evening 217 kilograms from the van were used at the night bakery. How many kilograms of flour remain in the first van?
w10_T4_001774: A drama club printed 207 programmes for its show. It threw away 24 that had come out of the printer smudged. Every remaining programme was sold at 3 pounds each on the night. The printing bill of 200 pounds was paid out of those takings. A patron then added 65 pounds to the same fund, and the costume hire took 308 pounds back out of it. The club has been putting on this show for a dozen seasons. How many pounds does the club have left?
w10_T4_001782: A branch library held 191 DVDs on its rack. An audit found 21 of them missing from their cases. A patron then donated 29 DVDs of her own. The autumn sale cleared 178 DVDs from the rack in a single weekend. Another 14 were sent across to the town library, and the branch records its loan periods in days rather than in weeks. The reading room next door seats 46 people. How many DVDs are left on the rack?
w10_T4_001784: A tiling firm had 237 boxes of slate in its yard and bought 8 more from a shop that was closing. Every box holds 4 tiles. A driver added 7 loose tiles that had been rattling about in his van. The whole stock was then shared equally between 3 building sites. Each tile delivered to the first site weighs 7 kilograms, and 33 kilograms of broken pieces were later swept up and carted away from that site. The firm bills its labour in minutes rather than hours. How many kilograms of slate does the first site have left?
w10_T4_001785: Hana brought 86 bulbs of garlic back from the farm. She discarded 15 of them that had gone soft in the bag. Her neighbour Petr, whose crop was smaller than Hana's, gave her 30 bulbs from his shed, and the market stall added 25 more. Every bulb she now has breaks into 4 cloves. Hana packed all of those cloves equally into 3 preserving jars, filling the blue jar first. How many cloves are in the blue jar?
w10_T4_001786: An orchard co-op started with 17 crates and lost 8 of them to rot damage. A neighbour lent it 17 crates, and the co-op bought 47 more at auction. Every crate it now owns was filled with 9 apples from the early harvest. Sorting then removed 93 apples that were badly bruised. The rest were packed equally onto 4 lorries, and the first lorry left at dawn. The orchard covers 38 hectares, and the co-op has been trading for a dozen years. How many apples were on the first lorry?
w10_T4_001790: A print works produced 206 posters on each of 3 days. Of those, 500 were posted out to shops around the county. Every poster still at the works was folded into 4 panels for the leaflet racks. Each panel carries printing on 2 sides. The works has 15 staff on the day shift. How many printed sides are there on the folded posters?
w10_T4_001794: A school stockroom held 139 exercise books. The office added 9 more, and a supplier sent another 22. Then 4 books were thrown out because their covers had been chewed. Every book in the stockroom contains 8 blank sheets, and the caretaker counted every sheet. The sheets were shared equally between 4 classes, Class Ash taking the first share, and 8 of Class Ash's sheets were later ruined by a leaking pen. The stockroom door has been sticking for a dozen weeks. How many sheets does Class Ash have left?
w10_T4_001800: Early in the morning a market gardener cut 81 bunches of stocks. Each bunch was tied from 9 stems. Every stem carried 3 open flowers when it was cut. In the afternoon a helper brought in 48 more flowers from the polytunnel. Just before closing that evening a customer returned 23 flowers that had not fitted in her vase. How many flowers does the gardener have altogether?
w10_T4_001809: A scout hut counted 35 board games in its cupboard. A jumble sale brought in another 35, and a family donated 23 more. A playgroup that was closing passed on a further 51 games. The whole collection was then shared equally between 4 huts in the district, with the Riverbank hut receiving the first share. The cupboard door has been broken for a dozen weeks. How many games went to the Riverbank hut?
w10_T4_001810: Nadia baked 19 scones on Sunday morning. She dropped 2 of them on the kitchen floor and had to bin them. Her brother Sam, who had baked far fewer than Nadia that weekend, ate 10 straight off the rack. She gave 2 more to the postman at the door. Another 3 went to the neighbours across the road, and Nadia writes her baking times in minutes rather than hours. How many scones does Nadia have left?
w10_T4_001818: A farm shop opened the morning with 73 punnets of strawberries. A grower's van added 41 more punnets before the doors opened. Every punnet on the shelf holds 6 strawberries. A picker dropped off 10 loose strawberries at midday for the tasting bowl. Through the afternoon and evening customers bought 455 strawberries in all. The shop has sold this variety for a dozen summers. How many strawberries are left in the shop?
w10_T4_001820: Miriam's depot holds 97 boxes, and each box contains 8 packs of stamp sheets. A courier delivered 9 more packs of exactly the same kind. Every pack holds 9 sheets. Her colleague Dev runs a second depot that holds twice as many sheets as Miriam's does now. Each sheet in Dev's depot carries 9 stamps. The post office then used 1058 of Dev's stamps in a single mailing. How many stamps does Dev's depot have left?
w10_T4_001823: A soup kitchen began the morning with 18 sacks of lentils and took delivery of 79 more. Every sack holds 9 kilograms. A grocer added 20 kilograms of loose lentils at midday, and a school harvest festival sent over 65 kilograms more. Through the afternoon the kitchen cooked with 664 kilograms of what it had. In the evening a wholesaler dropped off another 68 kilograms. The kitchen serves its meals at 12 long tables. How many kilograms of lentils does the kitchen hold now?
w10_T4_001825: A cycling club sold 161 tickets for its annual dinner in the first week. Another 57 went in the second week, and a further 75 were taken at the clubhouse door. Every ticket was priced at 5 pounds. The caterer's bill of 372 pounds came straight out of the ticket money. A member then handed in 37 pounds she had collected in a jar, and the club has run this dinner for a dozen years. How many pounds does the club have from the dinner?
w10_T4_001828: A pottery had 30 glazed jugs on its shelf and sent 18 of them to a gallery. Over the next month the number of jugs left on that shelf doubled. The potter then split the shelf's jugs equally between 3 market stalls. At the first stall 6 jugs were broken when a table collapsed. A new firing sent 41 jugs to that same stall, and by Sunday 37 of the stall's jugs had been sold. The kiln reaches 1200 degrees. How many jugs does the first stall have left?
w10_T4_001840: Ines began her collection with 54 postcards in a shoebox. Her friend Luca, who owns fewer than she does, gave her 22 from his own box. She then posted 54 of hers to family abroad. A market stall sold her 80 postcards in a single lot, and a cousin sent 15 more in an envelope. Her grandmother added 3 very old ones from the attic. Ines has been collecting for a dozen years. How many postcards does Ines have now?
w10_T4_001842: Early on Saturday morning Amira had 204 pots on her nursery bench, and she sold 85 of them straight away. Every pot still on the bench holds 5 seedlings. Her assistant Bruno, who had grown far fewer than Amira, added 26 loose seedlings from his own tray. During the afternoon a landscaper took 128 seedlings for a hedge planting. In the evening a school collected 157 more seedlings for its garden club. Amira has run this nursery for a dozen years. How many seedlings are left on the bench?
w10_T4_001843: A community trust owns 230 chairs and shares them equally between its 5 halls. The warden of the Elm hall, Mr. Chen, hired out every chair in his hall at 7 pounds each for a wedding. His colleague Ms. Rowe, whose hall took far less money that weekend, keeps her accounts separately. Repairs to the Elm hall floor cost 281 pounds out of that hire money, and a cleaning bill took another 32 pounds. The trust's minibus carries 17 passengers, and the halls are booked in minutes rather than hours. How many pounds does Mr. Chen have left from the hire?
w10_T4_001846: A baker had 57 loaves ready at first light and baked another 67 before the market opened. He divided the whole morning batch equally between 4 baskets. During the afternoon he supplied 4 stalls, making each stall's tray match one basket exactly, loaf for loaf. In the evening every loaf on those stalls sold for 7 pounds. The baker has kept this pitch for a dozen years. How many pounds did the evening's selling bring in?
w10_T4_001847: Priya rode 101 kilometres on each of 3 days at the start of her charity tour. On the fourth day she covered another 75 kilometres, and on the fifth she managed 78. A short evening loop added 5 kilometres to her total. Her friend Devan, who rode fewer kilometres than Priya on every single day, joined her for the final 25 kilometres, which she also added to her own tally. Priya's cycle computer reports distances in metres, though she writes them up in kilometres. How many kilometres has Priya ridden in total?
w10_T4_001850: On Monday morning a bookshop split 24 boxes equally between its 4 delivery vans. The driver of the first van, Tomas, then loaded 70 more boxes that had been waiting on the pavement. Every box in his van holds 9 books. During the afternoon Tomas delivered 265 books to schools around the county, while his colleague Ruth delivered far fewer from her own van. The bookshop's window display holds 48 titles. How many books are still in Tomas's van?
